full_judgment: 2. Shorts facts are that the pre-emptor instituted pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1986 subsequently renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 247 of 1977. Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1986 subsequently renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 246 of 1977 and Miscellaneous Case No. 32 of 1986 subsequently renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 1976 respectively against the common pre-emptee, Md. Nurul Haque Howlader for pre-emption of the case lands (181/2+ .13+ .211/4 decimals) measuring in total .53 decimals of land sold under three registered kabalas under section 96 of the E.B.S.A. and Tenancy Act, 1950 stating, inter alia, that the pre-emptor No.1 is a co-sharer in the case holdings recorded under S. h. Khatian Nos. 73, 74 and 75 on the basis of purchase vide registered kabalas dated 24.08.1972, 09.04.1974 and 07.06.1974 respectively. The pre-emptee, Md. Nurul Haque Howlader, being a stranger in the case holdings, purchased the same from other co-sharers by three registered kabalas dated 1305.1974, 12.08.1975 and 20.10.1975 without serving notices under section 89 of the E.B.S.A. and Tenancy Act upon the pre-emptor and other co-sharers. The pre-emptor on being aware of the aforesaid transfers from one Reboti Mohan Sil on 16th Bhaidra. 1384 B.S. obtained certified copy of the kabalas and came to learn about the transactions definitely on 05.09.1977,28.09.1977 and 09.01.1976. Accordingly he filed the aforesaid three cases for pre-emption of the case lands on depositing consideration money together with statutory compensation within 4 months from the respective dates of knowledge. The pre-emptee did not appear to contest the Miscellaneous proceedings, all the cases were at first allowed ex-parte on 17.07.1976 & 11.03.1978. On obtaining the ex-parte orders of pre-emption in his favour, the pre-emptor No.1 transferred the entire case lands to Mesbah Uddin, his son-in-law Kazi Abul Hossain and his two grand sons Kazi Altaf Hossain and Kazi Munir Hossain on different dates in the year 1979. Mesbahuddin again transferred his portion of the case lands of his daughter, Mosammat Mahmuda Begum by executing a deed of gift dated 16.02.1982. In the meantime the pre-emptee, Md. Nurul Haque Howlader filed three separate miscellaneous cases under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original pre-emption miscellaneous cases. Those cases were ultimately allowed on contest restoring all the original pre-emption cases to the respective files and numbers on 15.11.1986 and 29.04.1986. Thereafter, subsequent purchasers and transferees of the case lands, on their applications under Order 22 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, were added as pre-emptors-petitioners.
